q: In chloroplasts, which way do protons flow through ATP synthase, and where is the ATP released?
options: From the stroma into the lumen; ATP is released inside the thylakoid lumen for photolysis
From the lumen into the stroma; ATP is released into the stroma for the Calvin cycle
From the intermembrane space into the stroma; ATP is released into the cytoplasm
From the stroma into the cytoplasm; ATP is exported to fuel respiration
explanation: ATP synthase spans the thylakoid membrane with its catalytic head facing the stroma. H+ diffuse down their gradient from the lumen (high H+) to the stroma, driving ATP synthesis (photophosphorylation). The ATP appears exactly where it is needed – in the stroma – to convert GP to triose phosphate and to regenerate RuBP. (In mitochondria, ATP is likewise made on the matrix side.)
